rv.q: The production is full of pace and creepiness when it could so easily slide into the ridiculous.
This is a brilliant production; I can't wait for my next visit to the Old Vic, and I will be buying the book tomorrow!
The interweaving of the mysterious supernatural space so often overlooked in modern life seems to stay just out of reach of this production.
Folk horror with an urban twist
This production occasionally gestures towards that achievement but never truly captures it. The story survives the journey to the stage. The spell does not.
Whether you've read the original novel or have no knowledge of the story, this is a piece of theatre that will grip you from the start and stay in your mind for a long time.

--> “Say your prayers and be good, too, or Dead Papa Toothwort is coming for you.” Rooted in the South West, and with performers from across the region, the play at times veers into the same territory as Jez Butterworth’s Jerusalem . There is a common sense of impending doom firmly rooted in frailties within the human condition.

It’s never consistently scary enough (though the few moments where the play truly leans into terror are shocking and tremendous), nor really funny enough, with most of the jokes landing with a thud, feeling like duds cut out of Jez Butterworth’s Jerusalem .
Yet there's no avoiding the fact that this Bristol Old Vic production is thin on atmosphere and lacks a much-needed sense of place.
